**Goose** is not supported yet. This is a self-contained first contribution: the scaffold
writes the code, the fixtures and the registration, and what is left is the part below.

Read [`docs/writing-an-adapter.md`](../../docs/writing-an-adapter.md) first — it is the
whole workflow, and it is written for someone who has never seen this codebase.

## What Goose reads

- `.goosehints` at the project root, and in any directory in the hierarchy. Goose loads the
  configured context files from the working directory up to the repository root.
- `~/.config/goose/.goosehints` — global, applying to every session.

Local hints win over global ones on conflict. The format is plain text with Markdown-style
references; an `@file.md` reference inlines that file's contents.

**Documentation:** Goose — Providing hints to goose — https://goose-docs.ai/docs/guides/context-engineering/using-goosehints/
_(read 2026-09-04; re-read it before you file the precedence data, and put the date you
actually read it in `retrieved`.)_

## What to build

- **Adapter id:** `goose`
- **Artifact to generate:** `.goosehints` at the repository root
- **Rendering:** one concatenated file, like the Claude Code adapter
- **Resolution:** `additive` — local and global hints are both loaded; local wins a conflict

## The part that needs care

`.goosehints` has no comment syntax of its own, so decide deliberately what
`options.marker` does here: an HTML comment is invisible in rendered Markdown, but this file
is not strictly Markdown, and a marker Goose reads aloud as an instruction is worse than no
marker. Whatever you choose, `read()` has to strip it back off — the round-trip test will
catch you if it does not.

Also: `@`-prefixed references inline other files. Driftgate must never emit one. It would
make the generated file's meaning depend on a file Driftgate does not control, which is the
same class of problem as a nondeterministic render.

## Steps

```bash
driftgate adapter new goose          # prints the plan
driftgate adapter new goose --yes    # applies it
pnpm install && pnpm test           # green as generated
```

1. Hand-write `fixtures/goose/expected/` from the documentation above, **before** touching
   `write()`. A golden generated by the adapter it checks proves only that the adapter
   agrees with itself.
2. Implement `detect` → `read` → `write` until the golden passes byte-exact.
3. Fill in `packages/adapters/goose/src/docs.ts` — every placeholder there is `TODO`, and
   dated `1970-01-01` so an unverified claim cannot be mistaken for a verified one.
4. Run Goose against the generated config and confirm it actually loads. Say so in the PR,
   with the version you tested.
5. Add `goose` to `.driftgate/driftgate.yaml` and run `driftgate sync` — this repository
   dogfoods every adapter it ships. Commit the generated file with your change.

## Done when

- `pnpm verify` is clean and `fixtures/goose/expected/` was written by hand, from the docs
- `detect` fixtures: `positive/` detected, `negative/` not
- `src/docs.ts` carries a real source URL, a real `retrieved` date, and the Goose version
  you verified against
- You ran the real tool and it loaded the file

Ask anything in the comments — an unanswerable question here is a bug in this issue.
